pairs.difference: A: yellow hay is the one loud mass, set against muted brown dirt and pale cyan stripes, with a single red rope accent. The ground gives the eye a rest. B: saturated teal cover on streaky orange wood, plus pink and blue tabs, red pins, and a green and yellow sticker. Hue families are 6.22, above the real top of 5.83, and the wood shadow goes red-maroon. No area is quiet.
pairs.fix: Calm the wooden table to a muted light tan with soft brown shadows. Keep the teal book as the only strong color and reduce the stickers and tabs to two accent colors.

pairs.difference: A: red, gold and white cart on blue, with cream paving as a neutral rest and clear separate hue roles. B: the barrel staves, the ground and even the iron bands all fall into orange-brown and maroon. In the lens the iron turns purple-brown. Hue families are 2.32, below the real 2.97, and shadows lose chroma (0.49, the real floor). The wood is pushed to burnt orange, as on the generated desks in the lessons.
pairs.fix: Paint the barrel in natural honey-tan wood, not burnt orange. Make the iron bands neutral grey steel and the ground a pale dusty beige. Keep shadows soft brown rather than dark red.

pairs.difference: A: blue machine on magenta-violet with pink, green and yellow cans. Cool overall (warm share 0.03, low) but with clear hero and background roles, and shadows stay rich blue. B: the whole card is orange, amber and red-brown (warm share 0.999, above the real 0.87). The black lantern is tinted brown-maroon in the lens (subject chroma 0.056, below the real floor) and shadow chroma collapses to 0.34. There is no cool color anywhere.
pairs.fix: Add a cool counterweight: make the lantern metal blue-grey steel with cool highlights, and let shadows lean blue-violet instead of brown. Keep the orange only in the background and flame.

pairs.difference: A: cyan cream, pink rim and orange cone on a green wall. The hero is clearly louder than the wall and the accent roles are distinct, all within real ranges. B: blue-grey viewer against a blue and lavender city, nearly one hue from front to back. Background chroma 0.084 is below the real floor of 0.117, and the hero has no hue separation from the pale backdrop.
pairs.fix: Give the background a stronger, cleaner color separate from the hero, such as a warm sunset sky behind the blue viewer. Keep the buildings simple and clearly different in hue from the metal.

pairs.difference: A: red coach with yellow wheels on sand under a blue sky. It runs warm (0.70, slightly over the real top), but the red is a browned local color and the sand gives a rest. B: pure primary yellow and red cars on pure cobalt track. Subject chroma 0.173 is above the real top of 0.153, and everything is pushed to maximum hue with almost no muted material color.
pairs.fix: Lower the cars to a slightly softer enamel yellow and red, make the track a muted slate blue, and add grey wheels and steel so the eye has neutral areas.

pairs.difference: A: muted tan hat with a teal band on violet-magenta stripes. Background chroma 0.248 is above the real top of 0.217 and hue families 1.87 are below the real floor, so the card reads as a loud field plus one tan mass. B: coral sandals and yellow straps on turquoise, a clear complementary pairing with all measures in range and shadows staying rich orange-red.
pairs.fix: Reduce the magenta stripes to a softer, slightly less saturated purple so the background no longer outshouts the hat, and add a warmer leather variation to the crown.

pairs.difference: A: red guitar on a stage with blue and violet lights and cream floor. Many hues (6.46, at the top of the range), but shadows stay rich navy and crimson (kept 1.14). B: horse coat is uniform orange-chestnut and the fence and floor are the same orange. Shadows on the legs, mane and tail drop to near-black brown (kept 0.29, well below the real floor of 0.61), so the darks lose all color.
pairs.fix: Paint the dark mane, tail and legs in deep rich brown-violet instead of near-black. Make the fence and floor a paler, more neutral wood so the horse is the only orange mass.

pairs.difference: A: lime-olive cactus on orange waves and orange-yellow sand. Hero and background are both loud, with almost the whole background one warm family. Hue families 2.86 are just below the real floor and subject shadows go olive-yellow, pulled by the warm background. B: green slide, pink wall, cyan ladder and pool, pale tile. Hue roles are distinct, the tile gives a neutral rest, and shadows stay rich green.
pairs.fix: Keep the cactus a deeper natural green with cool blue-green shadows. Make the sand a pale muted beige and the background a separate cooler color so the card is not all orange and yellow.

pairs.difference: A: orange drink on violet, with a cyan umbrella and pink straw and clear glass neutrals. The background is loud (0.24, slightly over the real top), but the roles are clear. B: terracotta jug, orange wood and red-pink rings all sit in one warm family. Warm share is 1.0 (real top 0.87), hue families are 2.07, and shadows go dark red-brown. There is no cool or neutral area on the card.
pairs.fix: Make the background a cool teal or blue instead of pink-red, and the table a paler, more muted wood. Keep the clay jug as the only terracotta mass, with shadows that lean toward cool violet-brown.

pairs.difference: A: pure cobalt pillow on pink rings, a two-hue card with strong chroma (0.1875, near the real top) whose shadows stay rich blue. B: saturated blue door, orange frame, green ivy and a multicolor wreath with cream wall as a rest. Both are loud but both fit real ranges, and color gives no clear reason to choose.

A: red bandana on cyan with navy knots and white paisley. Two-hue and strong, sitting at the range edges (subject 0.190, hue families 1.94), but the white and navy accents give relief. B: orange and yellow towel on pure bright green (background 0.217, the real top). Hero and background are equally loud, the yellow stripes lean acid, and there is no neutral anywhere.
pairs.fix: Soften the green background to a calmer, slightly deeper green and add cream-white stripes to the towel so there is a neutral area to rest the eye.

pairs.difference: A: orange copper lamp on yellow-green rays. The glass picks up the background tint, and all measures are in range. B: nearly neutral grey steel pan with small gold nuggets on the same rays. Subject chroma 0.026 is below the real range, but grey steel is a believable local color and the lessons show generated cards pushing chroma up, not down. Color does not separate them.

pattern: Generated cards still give themselves away through warm-pulled local color. Wood, clay and coats go burnt orange or chestnut, and a shared warm family spreads across hero, ground and props (p02, p07, p09). Metals and blacks get tinted instead of staying neutral, and shadows fall to brown or maroon rather than shifting to related cool violet or blue-grey (p03, p07). Hero and background are equally loud, with no muted neutral area to rest the eye. Real cards keep true greys and off-whites, cooler shadow sides, and calmer ground planes.
